recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the current folder for drafts only. A non-author reviewer copies the exact approved file into a retention folder that only the three reviewers can write. The copy is named with the document and UTC approval time, and the reviewer records their account and that time beside it. Copies and records are kept for seven years, and later edits need a new approval and a new copy. Author write access to the retention folder must be removed before this week's first release. No optional additions are offered. Unmet needs: the reply has not seen the contract, the folder or its permissions, and the approver's account and time are entered by the reviewer rather than captured by the system.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires every released document to keep its exact approved version, the approver's identity, and the approval time for seven years; authors must not approve their own documents, and later edits must leave that retained version unchanged. You want those controls in place before this week's delivery, and you would prefer to keep the shared folder, add an APPROVED column of typed initials, and agree a naming convention.
labels.Deleted: The initials column and naming convention as the release control, and any new approval system. All twelve authors can edit the shared folder, so an initial is typed text, a renamed file can still be overwritten, and an author can mark their own document.
labels.Bottleneck: The approved file and the approval record still live where authors write. That is what fails the contract for this week's delivery.
labels.Checked myself: Your account of the contract, the twelve authors, the three reviewers, weekly releases, and author edit access. I have not seen the contract, the folder, or its permissions.

note: The reply uses access controls on existing tools: a reviewer-only retention folder holding exact copies plus an approver account and time record kept for seven years, which binds non-author approval to the exact version and protects it from authors.
